This market refers to the Counter-Strike Quarterfinal 2 match between G2 and Team Falcons in the BLAST Rivals Playoffs, initially scheduled for November 13, 2026 at 5:30 AM ET. This market will resolve to "G2" if G2 win Map 2 against Team Falcons. This market will resolve to "Team Falcons" if Team Falcons win Map 2 against G2. If the match begins but is not completed, and Map 2 is concluded with a winner determined, this market will resolve based on the completed Map 2. If Map 2 is not completed for any reason, this market will resolve 50-50. If the match is canceled (not played at all), this market will resolve 50-50. If the match is postponed, it must be rescheduled to a start time on or before November 27, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (14 calendar days after the originally scheduled start of November 13, 2026 at 5:30 AM ET). If, by that deadline, the most recently announced rescheduled start time is on or before the deadline, this market resolves based on the result of the match as played. Otherwise, this market resolves 50-50, regardless of whether the match is subsequently played. The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://hltv.org. This market will resolve according to the first individual who is officially announced as the successor to Jensen Huang as CEO of NVIDIA Corporation by December 31, 2028, 11:59 PM ET. An announcement of a successor will be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether the announced replacement actually becomes the next CEO of NVIDIA. Interim CEOs will not qualify. If no successor is announced by December 31, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Jensen Huang (No Change)”. The resolution source will be public statements from NVIDIA Corporation, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.NVIDIA's abrupt leadership shift, triggered by Jensen Huang's November 12 resignation amid reports of extramarital affairs including one involving national security concerns, has created a fluid succession race now led by interim CEO Colette Kress. Traders assign Ian Buck the highest implied probability among contenders due to his long tenure, CUDA platform leadership, and oversight of hyperscale AI hardware/software, positioning him to preserve the company's technical edge in large language models and accelerated computing. Kress offers continuity in operations, investor relations, and earnings oversight after over a decade as CFO, while external names like Rene Haas bring Arm expertise and broader industry perspective. The closely matched field reflects uncertainty over whether the board prioritizes engineering depth, financial stability, or outside regulatory savvy for the permanent role amid ongoing AI competition and geopolitical pressures.
